summary.text: A 56-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus under irregular medication and daily alcohol use presented to the emergency department with epigastric pain radiating to the back, vomiting, high-grade fever and productive cough for 5 days. On admission his GCS was 15/15, pulse rate 140 beats per min, blood pressure 80/60 mm Hg and respiratory rate 30/min, with epigastric tenderness, guarding and rigidity.

Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen showed peripancreatic inflammation, peritoneal fluid collection and bilateral pleural effusion, with a modified CT severity index of 6. Serum amylase was 2346 U/L and lipase 1256 U/L. He was diagnosed with acute severe alcoholic pancreatitis, diabetic ketoacidosis precipitated by right side community-acquired pneumonia, and septic shock with multi-organ dysfunction.

He was resuscitated with fluids and noradrenaline and started on piperacillin-tazobactam, doxycycline, insulin and ulinastatin 2 million units intravenously every twelve hours for 5 days. Noradrenaline was stopped on the third day, he was discharged from ICU on the sixth day and from the hospital on a ninth day, and at outpatient follow-up one week after discharge he was not having any symptoms.

summary.text: A 36-year-old man weighing 130 kg with type 2 diabetes mellitus, obstructive sleep apnea and hypertension under irregular medication and daily alcohol use presented to the emergency department with diffuse abdominal pain, vomiting, high-grade fever and burning micturition for 5 days. On admission his GCS was 15/15, pulse rate 126 beats per min, blood pressure 60/40 mm Hg and respiratory rate 34/min, with epigastric tenderness, guarding and rigidity.

Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen showed a normal enhancing pancreas with swollen head, body peripancreatic inflammation and fluid collection, with a modified CT severity index of 6. He was diagnosed with acute severe alcoholic pancreatitis, diabetic ketoacidosis precipitated by complicated urinary tract infection, and septic shock with multi-organ dysfunction.

He was resuscitated with fluids and noradrenaline and started on piperacillin-tazobactam, doxycycline, insulin and ulinastatin 2 million units intravenously every twelve hours for 5 days. Noradrenaline was stopped on the fourth day, he was discharged from ICU on the sixth day and from the hospital on an eighth day, and at outpatient follow-up one week after discharge he was not having any symptoms.

summary.text: A 76-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus, chronic obstructive airway disease, obstructive sleep apnea and hypertension under irregular medication, daily alcohol use and a 10 pack-year smoking history presented to the emergency department with epigastric pain, vomiting, high-grade fever, productive cough and shortness of breath. On admission her GCS was 10/15, pulse rate 110 beats per min, blood pressure 90/60 mm Hg and respiratory rate 34/min.

Chest x-ray showed bilateral lower zone pneumonia and contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen showed pancreatic necrosis in 30% with swollen neck and tail, with a modified CT severity index of 8. Serum amylase was 1956 U/L and lipase 1102 U/L. Diagnoses were acute severe alcoholic pancreatitis, acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive airway disease with type 2 respiratory failure precipitated by bilateral pneumonia, and septic shock with multi-organ dysfunction.

She was resuscitated with fluids and noradrenaline and started on piperacillin-tazobactam, doxycycline, BiPAP and ulinastatin 2 million units intravenously every twelve hours for 5 days. Noradrenaline was stopped on the fifth day, discharge from ICU was on the fifth day and from the hospital on an eighth day, and at outpatient follow-up one week after discharge there were no symptoms.

article_limitations: Case reports with no calendar dates; times are relative to admission or discharge only as stated.
Discussion statements about ulinastatin effects, mortality and published studies are general and not recorded as patient facts.
The statement that all patients had hypotension and acute kidney injury that resolved in 3-6 days is recorded for each patient without a patient-specific duration.
Several laboratory values are printed identically across cases (urea in all three cases; total protein in cases 1 and 2; amylase and lipase in cases 2 and 3); recorded as printed.
Case 2 noradrenaline dose unit is garbled in the source; case 3 uses she/her and he/his/him pronouns.
Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the three CT images are described in visual.json.
No supplements are listed for this article.

Figure 2 carries burned-in identifier text (a name-like line, a sex/age line and a partly cut-off date stamp; values not transcribed). Its printed age does not match the 36-year-old Case 2 patient; attribution to Case 2 rests only on the "(Figure 2)" callout in the Case 2 text.
Imaging, laboratory and diagnosis events carry no stated time and are ordered only where the source states order (presentation/admission and in-hospital care before the hospital discharge).
